about.title: Belmont Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Belmont's mix of shopping centers along El Camino Real, older sidewalks near Old County Road, and busy commercial parking lots off Ralston Avenue all create the everyday hazards that lead to falls: wet floors, cracked pavement, loose mats, poor lighting, and uneven curbs. When a fall happens on someone else's property, California law asks whether the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and failed to fix it or warn visitors. That question of "notice" often decides the entire claim, which is why documenting the hazard quickly matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge any fee. We simply connect Belmont residents and visitors who were hurt in a fall with an independent attorney from our network who can review the details, look into who's responsible, and explain your options in plain terms before any deadlines pass.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You File Anything

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Fast Work
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help identify what evidence establishes that before it disappears.

items.title: Surveillance Video Doesn't Last Long
items.desc: Many stores and businesses in Belmont overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Affect Your Recovery
items.desc: California is a pure comparative fault state, meaning even if you're found partly responsible, you may still recover a share of damages. An attorney can help present the facts fairly rather than let assumptions decide the outcome.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Belmont?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is government-owned, such as a public sidewalk or building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. Because these timelines are strict, it's worth talking to someone promptly.

items.question: I fell in a parking lot off Ralston Avenue and didn't take pictures. Is my claim over?
items.answer: Not necessarily. While photos and video help a great deal, other evidence like incident reports, maintenance records, and witness accounts can still support a claim. An attorney can advise on what's still available and how to request it.

items.question: Does it matter that I was partly distracted when I fell?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility for the fall. Your recovery may be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't automatically eliminated. An attorney can help explain how this might apply to your specific situation.
